question: Under s. 452.19(1m)(a), a licensee generally may not pay a fee, commission, or referral/finder's fee to a person who is not licensed under ch. 452. Which of the following is a valid exception described in this provision?
choice_a: A person who is a licensed attorney assisting with the transaction
choice_b: A person who was licensed under ch. 452 when the commission was earned or when the referral fee arrangement was made, and who is regularly and lawfully engaged in the real estate brokerage business in another state, territory, or foreign country
choice_c: A close relative of the paying licensee
choice_d: Any unlicensed assistant employed by the firm
explanation: Section 452.19(1m)(a) bars payment to unlicensed persons unless that person was licensed under ch. 452 when the commission was earned or referral arrangement made, or is regularly and lawfully engaged in the real estate brokerage business in another state, territory, or foreign country.

question: If a licensee is associated with a firm, to whom must all fees, commissions, and compensation for a referral or finder's fee for acts specified in ch. 452 be paid, under s. 452.19(1m)(b)?
choice_b: Directly to the individual licensee who performed the work
choice_c: To the Department of Safety and Professional Services for distribution
choice_d: Split equally between the licensee and the firm
explanation: Section 452.19(1m)(b) states that if a licensee is associated with a firm, all such fees, commissions, and referral/finder's fee compensation shall be paid to the firm.

question: A residential real estate transaction involves a property with 1 to 4 dwelling units. Under s. 452.19(3)(a), a firm generally may not accept compensation of any kind from another firm in connection with brokerage services performed as part of that transaction. This prohibition applies:
choice_a: Only if both firms represent the same party
choice_b: Only when no cooperative agreement exists
choice_c: Regardless of whether the firms represent different parties (such as buyer and seller) or whether a non-listing firm is acting as a buyer's agent, subagent, or in another cooperative capacity
explanation: Section 452.19(3)(a)2 specifies the prohibition applies regardless of whether the firms represent different parties or whether a non-listing firm acts as a buyer's agent, subagent, or in another cooperative capacity.

question: Which type of firm-to-firm payment is expressly NOT prohibited by s. 452.19(3) in a transaction involving a 1-4 unit residential property?
choice_a: A commission split negotiated at closing
choice_d: A referral fee or finder's fee as described in sub. (1m)
explanation: Section 452.19(3)(a)3 states that the prohibition in subd. 1. does not prohibit payment of compensation for a referral fee or finder's fee as described in sub. (1m).

question: What is the legal effect, under s. 452.19(3)(b), of an agreement or arrangement that violates the firm-to-firm compensation prohibition in sub. (3)?
choice_b: It is voidable only at the buyer's request
choice_c: It remains enforceable but subject to a fine
choice_d: It must be renegotiated within 30 days
explanation: Section 452.19(3)(b) provides that any agreement or arrangement that violates the subsection is void and unenforceable.

question: In a transaction involving a residential property with 1 to 4 dwelling units, a seller agrees to pay compensation to a firm that is not the listing firm for brokerage services provided to the buyer. Under s. 452.19(4)(a), this agreement must:
choice_a: Be verbally confirmed by the seller's attorney
choice_b: Be recorded with the county register of deeds
choice_c: Be expressly stated in the fully executed offer to purchase or option to purchase and signed by both the buyer and the seller
choice_d: Be approved in advance by the Real Estate Examining Board
explanation: Section 452.19(4)(a) requires such an agreement to be expressly stated in the fully executed offer to purchase or option to purchase and signed by the buyer and the seller as part of the contract.

question: Under s. 452.19(4)(b), a firm that is not the listing firm may receive compensation from a party to the transaction who is not its client only if:
choice_b: The buyer waives the requirement in writing
choice_c: The compensation is less than 3% of the sale price
choice_d: The agreement to pay the compensation is documented in the executed offer to purchase or option to purchase
explanation: Section 452.19(4)(b) states a non-listing firm may not receive compensation from a party who is not its client unless the agreement to pay is documented in the executed offer to purchase or option to purchase.

question: Under s. 452.19(4)(d), what must a listing contract include regarding compensation offered to firms other than the listing firm?
choice_a: A statement as to whether the seller authorizes the listing firm to disclose that the seller is offering compensation to a firm other than the listing firm
choice_b: A cap on the amount of compensation that may be offered
choice_c: A requirement that all such compensation be paid through escrow
choice_d: A waiver of the seller's right to negotiate commission
explanation: Section 452.19(4)(d) requires a listing contract to include a statement as to whether the seller authorizes the listing firm to disclose if the seller is offering compensation to a firm other than the listing firm.

question: Under s. 452.20, a person may not bring or maintain a court action in Wisconsin for collection of a commission or compensation for an act described in ch. 452 unless that person:
choice_a: Files the claim within 30 days of the transaction closing
choice_b: Alleges and proves that he or she was a duly licensed broker or salesperson at the time the alleged cause of action arose
choice_c: Obtains a certificate from the Department of Safety and Professional Services
choice_d: Proves the client benefited financially from the services rendered
explanation: Section 452.20 requires a person to allege and prove that he or she was a duly licensed broker or salesperson at the time the alleged cause of action arose in order to maintain an action for a commission.

question: Under s. 452.21, in any prosecution for violation of ch. 452, what does proof that a person acted as a broker or salesperson establish?
choice_a: Conclusive proof that the person violated the licensing law
choice_b: Proof that the person's license was suspended
choice_c: Prima facie proof that compensation for the acts was received or promised
choice_d: Nothing, absent a signed listing agreement
explanation: Section 452.21 provides that proof a person acted as a broker or salesperson is prima facie proof that compensation therefor was received or promised.

question: Under s. 452.22, a certificate from the chairperson of the board stating that a specified individual was not the holder of a broker's license on a specified date is:
choice_a: Prima facie evidence of the facts stated in the certificate for all purposes in any action or proceeding
choice_b: Inadmissible without live testimony from the chairperson
choice_c: Only admissible in disciplinary hearings, not civil actions
explanation: Section 452.22(2) states that such a certificate is prima facie evidence of the facts stated in the certificate for all purposes in any action or proceeding.

question: A licensee ceases to be associated with a firm. Under s. 452.30(4)(a), within how many days after ceasing association must the licensee send written notice to the department?
explanation: Section 452.30(4)(a) requires the licensee to send written notice to the department within 10 days after the date the licensee ceases to be associated with the firm.

question: Under s. 452.30(7), which statement correctly describes a salesperson's association with a firm?
choice_a: A salesperson may be associated with multiple firms simultaneously, as long as each is notified
choice_b: A salesperson may be associated with only one firm at a time and may not engage in independent real estate practice
choice_c: A salesperson may engage in independent real estate practice once licensed for 3 years
choice_d: A salesperson is not required to be associated with any firm
explanation: Section 452.30(7) states a salesperson may be associated with only one firm at a given time and may not engage in independent real estate practice, engaging in real estate practice only when associated with a firm.

question: Under s. 452.38(1)(b), for a licensee's compensation arrangement to help satisfy the independent contractor test, what portion of the compensation related to sales or other output (measured on a calendar year basis) must be directly related to the brokerage services the licensee performed on behalf of the firm?
explanation: Section 452.38(1)(b) requires that 75% or more of the compensation related to sales or other output, measured on a calendar year basis, be directly related to the brokerage services performed by the licensee on behalf of the firm.

question: A firm arranges for a licensed broker who provides no actual services to act as a conduit so that a fee can be passed to an unlicensed person for locating a buyer. According to the case annotation under s. 452.19 (Badger III Ltd. Partnership v. Howard, Needles, Tammen & Bergendoff), this arrangement:
choice_a: Does not create a co-brokerage arrangement authorized by the statute, because an agreement to pay a commission to an unlicensed person is void at its inception under s. 452.03
choice_b: Creates a valid co-brokerage arrangement authorized by s. 452.19
choice_c: Is permitted because the licensed broker signed the agreement
choice_d: Is valid as long as the unlicensed person discloses the arrangement to the buyer
explanation: The annotation explains that under s. 452.03 an agreement to pay a commission to a person not licensed as a broker is void at its inception, and using a licensed broker who provides no actual services as a conduit does not create an authorized co-brokerage arrangement.
source_note: Wis. Stat. 452.19, case annotation citing Badger III Ltd. Partnership v. Howard, Needles, Tammen & Bergendoff, 196 Wis. 2d 891 (Ct. App. 1995)
